paper.title: Managing Self-Learning Experts under Per-Round Budget Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Decision making with trainable experts under per-round learning budget M
unmapped: Experts are self-learning: each expert improves only when selected for training; at most M experts trained per round, one deployed
Each expert satisfies a known anytime high-probability regret envelope U_k(n,delta) relative to its own optimum L_k^*
Deployed decision built by a smoothing wrapper over the deployed expert's history
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, $\mathcal{P}$ allocates the training budget to a subset $S_t \subseteq [K]$ (where $|S_t| \le M$) and selects a global decision $u^t \in \mathbf{U}$ by adopting the advice of a chosen expert. ... The loss is $\ell:\mathbf{U}\times \mathbf{E}\to [0,1].$

settings.name_in_paper: Single-deployment setting with K experts solving alpha-hard tasks (lower bound)
unmapped: Each expert is itself a bandit learner (two-armed heavy-tailed bandit) trained only when selected; at most M experts updated per round
settings.definition_quote: Consider the single-deployment setting of Section~\ref{sec:losses} with $K$ experts, horizon $T$, and a per-round budget $M$.

symbols.M: per-round training budget (number of experts trained per round)
symbols.alpha_rate: exponent of experts' regret envelope U_k(t,delta)=O(t^alpha c(delta)), alpha in (0,1)
symbols.c_delta: problem-dependent confidence scaling c(delta), polylogarithmic in 1/delta for standard experts

conditions: each expert satisfies Assumption 2 with U_k(t,delta)=O(t^alpha c(delta))
tuning: confidence bounds of Definition 1 with confidence delta

source.label: thm:gen-rate
source.quote: Let $\alpha, \delta \in (0, 1)$ and each expert $k$ satisfy Asm.~\ref{assumption:expert_regret} with $U_k(t,\delta) =O\big(t^{\alpha}c(\delta)\big)$... Then, with probability at least $1 - \delta$ the regret of Alg.~\ref{algorithm:M_LCB} is bounded for all $T\ge1$ as $\mathrm{Reg}(T) = O\left(\sqrt{\frac{K T}{M}\log(\frac{KT}{\delta})} + \Bigl(\tfrac{K}{M}\Bigr)^{1-\alpha} T^{\alpha} c(\delta)\right).$

results.notes: Regret is realized loss minus T*L^* against best expert's optimum. Holds for all T simultaneously.

bound.regime: sqrt(K log K/(M T)) sufficiently small

symbols.alpha_rate: hardness exponent of the expert task class F_alpha, alpha in [0,1]

conditions: each expert solves a problem from a class F_alpha admitting an alpha-regret lower bound (Def. 2)
for alpha > 1/2 losses are non-negative heavy-tailed with bounded (1+beta)-moment, alpha=1/(1+beta); for alpha <= 1/2 Bernoulli losses suffice; alpha=1 uses [0,1] losses with T+1 arms
constants c1, c2 depend only on alpha

source.label: thm:mt-alpha
source.quote: There exists a class $\mathcal F_\alpha$ satisfying Def.~\ref{def:alpha-class}, s.t. if each expert $k \in [K]$ solves a problem $f_k \in \mathcal F_\alpha$, then, for sufficiently small $\sqrt{\frac{K\log K}{MT}}$ and for any algorithm $\mathscr{A}_k$ and meta-procedure $\mathcal{P}$ $\sup \mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{Reg}(T) \ge c_1\,\sqrt{\frac{K\,T}{M}} + c_2\,T^\alpha \left(\frac{K}{M} \right)^{1-\alpha}$

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 4 in the appendix (not recorded separately). E Reg(T) equals expected loss minus T L^*, i.e. pseudo-regret. Holds for any expert algorithms and meta-procedure.

symbols.alpha_rate: exponent of experts' regret envelope, alpha in (0,1]

conditions: each expert satisfies Assumption 2 with U_k(t,delta)=O(t^alpha c(delta))
regret is the top-M mean regret Reg_M(T)=sum_t [ (1/M) sum_{k in S_t} L_k^* - min_{|S|=M} (1/M) sum_{k in S} L_k^* ]

source.label: thm:gen-rate-topM
source.quote: Let $\alpha\in(0,1]$, $\delta\in(0,1)$. Let each expert $k$ satisfy Asm.~\ref{assumption:expert_regret} with $U_k(t,\delta)=O\big(t^{\alpha}c(\delta)\big)$. Run Alg.~\ref{algorithm:M_LCB} ... Then, with probability at least $1 - \delta$ ... $\mathrm{Reg}_M(T)= O\left(\sqrt{\frac{KT}{M}\log\frac{KT}{\delta}} + \Bigl(\frac{K}{M}\Bigr)^{1-\alpha} T^{\alpha} c(\delta)\right).$

results.notes: Multiple-play variant: comparator is the best subset of M experts (not expressible exactly; best_expert used).
